wv_a_fern_point.blurb: Fern Point Slabs is one of the sectors of Endless Wall, the best-known cliff line in the New River Gorge. The 26 climbs here are split fairly evenly between sport and trad, on sandstone. Difficulty leans hard: most routes fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a handful of 5.9s and 5.10s for those warming up and a couple of 5.13s at the top end. This is not a beginner's cliff, so it suits climbers already comfortable leading in the 5.11 range who want a mix of bolted and gear-protected lines in one spot.

wv_orange_oswald_wall.blurb: Orange Oswald Wall is a busy sport wall at Summersville Lake, in the state park near Summersville. Most of its 26 climbs are bolted lines, with a few trad routes and two easy boulder problems. Grades cluster around 5.10, with plenty of 5.9s and some 5.11s, and one or two easier lines for newer leaders. It is a place to spend a day on moderate sport routes. The wall is exposed and catches sun nearly all day, so summer can be hot, while a calm winter day can be pleasant. Views over the water add to the setting. Reaching the base means taking a ladder and following a trail along the shore.

wv_circus_wall.blurb: Circus Wall is a compact sport-climbing wall in the main area at Summersville Lake, close to Orange Oswald Wall. Of its 25 climbs, most are bolted sport lines and four are trad. The grades start around 5.9 and are concentrated in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with one 5.13. That makes it a good stop for climbers who have outgrown the easier walls nearby and want a dense group of harder routes in one spot. The lake setting means a short walk in from the state park lot.

wv_08_ames_wall.blurb: Ames Wall is a sector of Bubba City, one of the most visited crags in the New River Gorge near Fayetteville. It is mainly a sport wall, with 23 of its 25 climbs bolted and a pair of trad lines. Grades span from 5.6 up to a single 5.13, but the bulk sit in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners. The wall lies a short stroll from the Bubba City downclimb approach, and it is set between the Central Bubba and Head Wall sectors.

_expect.name: The Diamond and The Cave Area

wv_the_diamond_and_the_cave_area.blurb: The Diamond and The Cave Area is a cluster of boulders at Coopers Rock State Forest in northern West Virginia. It belongs to the In-Between Area, along the boulder trail past the Roadside zone. Nearly all of the 25 climbs are boulder problems on sandstone, with one trad line. Grades run widely, from easy to very hard, but the middle is solid V3 to V4 territory with several harder projects and a few high-end lines. A big overhanging block and a cave anchor the zone. Holds can be fragile, so wait for dry rock.

wv_4_moon_wall.blurb: 4 Moon Wall is one of the quieter cliffs in the Lower Meadow, in the Meadow River Gorge of the New River Gorge region. It sits on the cliff line after The Greatest Show area, beyond a waterfall and an orange arete. The 25 climbs are overwhelmingly trad, with a couple of sport lines. Grades begin around 5.5 and run to 5.12, with the greatest number in the 5.6 to 5.8 range. The Lower Meadow in general gets a bit more sun than shade, and you reach this wall by a trail walk up from the gravel lot.

wv_main_area_3.blurb: Main Area is the biggest and densest boulder cluster along the Rocky Ridge Trail in the Dolly Sods region of eastern West Virginia, at roughly 4,100 feet. All 26 problems are bouldering on sandstone. The grades are friendly: most sit between V0 and V3, with the most common being V2, and a small number of harder problems reaching V6 and a single V8 at the top. The boulders surround you as you walk the ridge trail, so there is no separate approach to the base. A smaller boulderfield lies a short walk to the north.
